title: Reduce TTFT variance by adjusting adaptive hedge scheduler and prefetch backoff
creator: Priya Nambiar
description: Multiple customers reported increased time-to-first-token (TTFT) and tokens/sec variance after the kernel scheduling change (runtime-1.20.3) that introduced the adaptive hedge scheduler. The regression appears across hosted and dedicated deployments but is most visible for multi-tenant Dedicated clusters and for models using mixed quantization (int8 + fp16 attention kernels). Symptoms: intermittent long TTFT tails (200-800ms extra), 20-40% drop in sustained tokens/sec during 5-15s bursts, and higher variance on requests with heterogeneous context windows. Root cause hypothesis: the adaptive hedge scheduler weight update path is overreacting to transient queue spikes and triggering aggressive prefetch cancellation; combined with a new prefetch backoff heuristic this causes occasional serial kernel selection fallbacks for certain quantized kernels, effectively losing parallelism for the first tokens. This ticket tracks triage, customer mitigation, and a minimal risk patch to stabilize TTFT while we build a more robust scheduler.
steps_taken: 03/10: Triage call with SRE, runtime, and product to collect telemetry and customer traces
03/10: Enabled detailed sampling of scheduler decisions and prefetch events in prod for affected clusters
03/11: Reproduced tail TTFT in a staging cluster by simulating mixed-size fanout and cold worker priming
03/12: Rolled a temporary config change to increase prefetch_backoff_ms from 50 to 150 for two Dedicated clusters; observed partial improvement
03/13: Deployed debug build that logs kernel selection reasons and hedge weights; collected 48 hours of traces
03/14: Drafted minimal change: clamp hedge weight deltas and add per-tenant prefetch hysteresis; running canary in hosted us-west-2
Customer comms: Sent interim note to affected customers with mitigation steps and ETA for patch
reproduction_steps: 1) Use a multi-tenant Dedicated cluster with at least 8 concurrent sessions across 3 model variants, including an int8-quantized variant
2) Issue a burst (100 requests over 10s) with mixed prompt lengths (50-2k tokens) and ensure overlapping cold-starts
3) Observe scheduler logs: look for rapid hedge weight oscillation >0.4 delta within 1s and prefetch cancellations
4) Measure TTFT distribution: tails above 300ms indicate the issue reproduced
notes: Trade-off: clamping hedge deltas reduces responsiveness to genuine congestion spikes; acceptable temporary trade while we add stability metrics

Decision: prioritize a conservative clamp + tenant hysteresis as a short-term remediation. Longer-term plan is to decouple kernel fallback penalties from hedge recalculation and add quantization-aware kernel probing
Follow-up: add an automated test that simulates heterogeneous context windows to catch regressions in CI
Design feedback: PM suggests exposing a per-customer 'prefetch aggressiveness' knob for Dedicated customers in Console
SRE ask: after canary, run a 24h soak with traffic replay from 2026-03-09 15:00 UTC
acceptance_criteria: Canary in hosted us-west-2 shows median TTFT no worse than baseline and 95th percentile improved by >=30% compared to pre-patch traces
Dedicated canary cluster shows sustained tokens/sec regression resolved under 1% deviation during 30-minute bursts
No increase in kernel OOM or other errors observed in canary logs
Customer escalations have been updated with timeline and mitigation steps

03/14-03/15: monitor canary for 24h with nightly soak and SLO gates

03/17: begin work on kernel-probing decoupling and add CI simulation for heterogeneous contexts
